aria: Animated recap of the Knicks' 97 to 96 home win over the Trail Blazers: Mikal Bridges' 3-pointer at the buzzer off Josh Hart's inbounds pass that turned a 96 to 94 deficit into the win, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jalen Brunson's 30 points, the top scorers, how the Knicks won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Knicks' 97–96 home win over the Portland Trail Blazers on Nov 21, 2026, from the Covers box score, checked line for line against the CBS Sports gametracker box score. All 97 New York points and all 96 Portland points add up from the player lines. The quarter scores (40–26–15–16 to 23–20–29–24) add up to both totals: New York led 66–43 at the half (Covers; AP) and 81–72 after three. Points in the paint (26–48), fast-break points, and both biggest leads (New York 26, Portland 2) are from Covers; threes (19–11), assists (25–21), blocks (8–7), rebounds (47–59 including team rebounds) and free throws (4 of 6 to 13 of 17) are from the CBS box score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games.

The Knicks' lead reached 26 on a Landry Shamet 3-pointer with 11 seconds left in the first half (New York Daily News via Yahoo). Jalen Brunson scored 19 of his 30 in the first quarter (AP; Daily News), and Portland outscored New York 29–15 in the third (AP) and 53–31 after halftime (Daily News; ClutchPoints). The Knicks went without a field goal for the final 5:25 of regulation until Bridges' shot (Daily News). Portland took its first lead of the game on Deni Avdija's free throws with 3.2 seconds left, 96–94 (Field Level Media; Reuters via GMA; Daily News; the AP says 3.4 seconds). New York won its fourth straight (AP; Daily News). Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) and OG Anunoby (left calf) sat for the first time this season (Daily News). The Knicks host Indiana on Sunday, Nov 22 at 8:00 PM ET (Covers; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Mikal Bridges' 3-pointer at the buzzer (AP: "Josh Hart found Bridges on the wing as Toumani Camara leapt past him"; Field Level Media and Reuters: Bridges took one dribble, pivoted past Camara and hit a fallaway 3 as time expired; the Daily News calls it a step-back 3). After Avdija's free throws, New York used its last timeout to advance the ball (AP; Field Level Media). The board's Blazers +2 to Knicks +1 is 94–96 to 97–96. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc; the one dribble, the fallaway and the exact spot on the wing are not drawn. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the New York Knicks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Mikal Bridges' listed 6-foot-6 and 209 pounds with No. 25 (RealGM; Wikipedia); no wingspan from a sourced measurement was found, so his arms use the standard proportion. He is drawn in New York's home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
